question: Should OpenClaw sponsor official FreeBSD support, and if so should it start as experimental/community support or Tier 1 release support?
rationale: The request crosses product tier, release packaging, CI, service management, docs, and long-term ownership; current main and the latest release intentionally document and validate other platform paths instead.

options.title: Define experimental FreeBSD scope first
options.body: Approve only a staged plan that names the FreeBSD package/ports owner, installer/update path, service manager, docs, and release-smoke expectations before any support claim is advertised.

options.title: Promote FreeBSD to Tier 1
options.body: Accept ongoing FreeBSD release ownership and split the work into tracked implementation tasks for packaging, service management, CI, docs, and validation.

options.title: Decline official FreeBSD support
options.body: Keep FreeBSD as community/source/npm use only and close this support-tier request after documenting that policy.

recommendation.title: Define experimental FreeBSD scope first
recommendation.body: Approve only a staged plan that names the FreeBSD package/ports owner, installer/update path, service manager, docs, and release-smoke expectations before any support claim is advertised.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses product tier, installer publication, release validation, and official support scope, and @steipete is the documented project lead with installer ownership history.
